operator.quote: ESS completed the transition from ESS AB to European Spallation Source ERIC on 1 October 2015

beam_power.quote: The world's most intense pulsed spallation neutron source, the European Spallation Source (ESS), will have a proton linac operating at 5\,MW power, 2\,GeV kinetic energy and 14~Hz repetition rate

proton_energy.quote: will have a proton linac operating at 5\,MW power, 2\,GeV kinetic energy and 14~Hz repetition rate

summary.plain: The world's most powerful planned neutron source, being built in Lund, Sweden, around a 5-megawatt proton linear accelerator. Its protons will make neutrons for materials research and could also drive a neutrino beam.
summary.technical: European Spallation Source (ESS ERIC), Lund, Sweden: 5 MW, 2 GeV proton linac at 14 Hz, under construction since September 2014; beam on tuning dump achieved May 2025; the ESSnuSB study proposes doubling the repetition rate and adding an accumulator ring for a neutrino super beam.
